On running badly

I started running at thirty-two and I'm still bad at it. Like, really bad — my best 5k is thirty-one minutes and I was proud of it for a whole month.

The thing nobody tells you is that being bad is kind of freeing. Nobody expects anything, I don't expect anything, so every run is just me and a podcast and my knees complaining. I think if I was good I'd care about pace and splits and all that, and honestly I'd probably quit.

So I keep running badly, three times a week, in the rain mostly because this is Poland. In conclusion, being bad at something on purpose is underrated, try it.
